news.title: Pune town planning schemes’ future in the dark as state cancels plans
news.para: Pune's town planning schemes face a bleak outlook as the state government has paused their progression. Some of these projects were already in the land acquisition phase, and the recent transition of two schemes in Uruli-Phursungi to a different municipal council only adds to the uncertainty. Urban development experts argue that this move could hinder the city's urgent urbanisation goals, even as other plans await action from PMRDA.

news.title: Freehold relief in sight for Chandigarh’s leasehold properties
news.para: The Ministry of Home Affairs is currently reviewing a proposal to convert leasehold properties to freehold status. This pivotal development emerges after extensive discussions among political figures and ministers. The Chandigarh administration, having secured the needed approvals, forwarded this proposal. It is anticipated that this change will enhance property values and stimulate investment within the city, along with providing updates on other property-related matters.

news.title: Registration opens for 460 plots in Lucknow development body's Anant Nagar
news.para: Online registration for 460 plots in Lucknow's Anant Nagar scheme is now open.  These plots, ranging from 112.5 to 200 square metres, will be allotted through a lottery.  The Anant Nagar scheme is being developed along Mohan Road with wide roads and green spaces.  LDA will also conduct a lottery for 407 housing units on August 14.  Previously, the authority allotted 75 flats in Park View and Aishbagh Square apartments.

news.title: Andhra Pradesh rolls out fresh incentives for IGBC-certified green projects
news.para: Andhra Pradesh has rolled out new concessions on development fees specifically tailored for green buildings. Developers of silver-rated projects will receive a five percent discount, while those achieving a gold rating can look forward to a ten percent reduction. Platinum-rated projects are rewarded handsomely with a fifteen percent concession.

news.title: Birla Estates' subsidiary buys FSI from Parinee entities for ₹159 crore
news.para: Birla Estates has successfully acquired almost 90,000 sq ft of FSI for over Rs 159 crore, a strategic move aimed at bolstering their society redevelopment efforts in Khar, Mumbai. This FSI was secured via a Slum Rehabilitation Authority scheme from Kandivali. The development rights will be transferred and applied to a larger property in Khar, enhancing the region's premium living environment.

news.title: Dream Finders to buy Beazer Homes in $2.2-billion deal
news.para: Dream Finders Homes is set to acquire Beazer Homes in a substantial $2.2 billion all-cash transaction, marking a pivotal expansion in Dream Finders' footprint within the housing sector. Shareholders of Beazer will receive $33.50 cash for each share held, while the deal is anticipated to finalize by the end of the fourth quarter in 2026, bringing a conclusion to extensive talks between the two firms.

news.title: Chennai metro rail phase-II 54% complete
news.para: Chennai Metro Rail Phase-II has achieved 54.62% physical progress on its extensive network. The Union government has released over ₹14,545 crore for the project's ongoing construction. This funding is directly linked to Chennai Metro Rail Ltd's requirements and the project's pace. The ₹63,246 crore project includes three major corridors and significant underground sections.

news.title: Survey finds 1,200 dilapidated structures, Nashik civic body demolishes 18 wadas
news.para: The Nashik Municipal Corporation is taking urgent measures to demolish hazardous structures. Within just fifteen days, they have successfully dismantled eighteen unsafe buildings. An extensive survey revealed twelve hundred dilapidated structures at risk. Despite official notices and prior incidents, many of these buildings remain occupied, largely due to complicating landlord-tenant disputes that hinder redevelopment efforts.

news.title: Bhubaneswar civic body seeks reply from builder over high-rise building in airport funnel path
news.para: The Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation has requested a formal explanation from a real estate company regarding a hotel project that surpassed its authorized height limit. Airport authorities identified this violation during an obstacle limitation survey. The developer has been issued a notice for exceeding the allowed elevation by more than eleven meters. The next steps will be determined pending the company's response.

news.title: Vadodara civic body extends advance property tax rebate scheme till September 10
news.para: The Vadodara Municipal Corporation has announced an extension of its property tax rebate scheme until September 10. Homeowners can take advantage of an 11 percent rebate if they make their payments online. Additionally, commercial property owners can benefit from a 6 percent rebate. So far, the civic body has successfully collected over Rs 186 crore through this advance tax initiative.

news.title: MMRDA ropes in Singapore’s Surbana Jurong for Mumbai 3.0 master plan
news.para: Singapore's Surbana Jurong will prepare the Mumbai 3.0 new town master plan. This new town will span over 323 square kilometers across Raigad district. The planning process involves detailed analysis and stakeholder consultations for development. Maharashtra's Deputy Chief Minister highlighted global expertise for this project. Mumbai 3.0 aims to be a sustainable and investment-ready global growth center.

news.title: Goa government allows citizens to register property document at any sub-registrar office in district
news.para: Goa has introduced property document registration at any Sub-Registrar Office within districts. This new facility aims to enhance access and reduce citizen waiting times significantly. Senior citizens and NRIs will benefit from increased flexibility and reduced travel needs. The initiative is expected to distribute workload evenly and improve service efficiency.

news.title: Dharwad consumer panel orders builder to refund 83 plot buyers with 10% interest
news.para: In a significant ruling, a consumer commission has mandated a Hubballi developer to refund 83 buyers who purchased plots in the failed Sai Ram City layout. Despite receiving deposits and installment payments over two years, the developer neglected the promised development. The commission identified service deficiencies and unfair practices, ordering the developer to return the full amount with 10% annual interest and additional compensation.

news.title: Andhra Pradesh government clears pilot slum redevelopment project in Visakhapatnam
news.para: The government of Andhra Pradesh has green-lighted the Velampeta slum redevelopment initiative in Visakhapatnam. This innovative project operates under a public-private partnership and a Design, Build, Finance, Transfer framework. Families from economically weaker sections will be relocated within the same area, while Transferable Development Rights will help to fill the funding void.

news.title: Eye on high-rise work resumption, builders in Kolkata start calling back workers to sites
news.para: In Kolkata, construction developers are bringing laborers back to the sites as many halted projects gain the necessary approvals to restart. Contractors are reaching out to the workers who had previously returned home, signaling a resurgence in construction activity expected in just weeks. The industry is positive about the government's newly implemented safety standards, seeing them as a boost to the sector.

news.title: Decades-old dispute buries ₹2,000-crore land under mountains of rubble in Hyderabad’s IT hub
news.para: In Hyderabad, a valuable land parcel worth over Rs 2,000 crore has tragically turned into a neglected dumpsite filled with construction waste. Entangled in a longstanding legal battle between a real estate firm and the state government, this land's value skyrocketed from Rs 50 lakh per acre. Now, it hosts massive heaps of debris, prompting the Cyberabad Municipal Corporation to seek effective, scientific solutions for waste clearance.

news.title: Delhi government reiterates no existing houses in O-Zone will face demolition action
news.para: The Delhi government confirmed that there are no plans to demolish any existing O-Zone houses. They pointed to current demolitions, requesting legal safeguards for colonies. Delhi Development Minister Kapil Mishra labeled the O-Zone situation as serious, assuring that more than thirty lakh homes are secure.

news.title: Beijing further relaxes home-buying curbs in property boost bid
news.para: Beijing officials have introduced new regulations to simplify home-buying processes. Families from outside Beijing can now acquire properties within the Fifth Ring Road after a year of tax or social insurance contributions. Additionally, first-time buyers will benefit from increased limits on housing provident fund loans, marking a significant shift in the local market dynamics.

news.title: The Ramco Cements' profit slumps 63% to ₹31 crore in Q1 FY27
news.para: Ramco Cements experienced a significant profit decline of more than sixty percent in the June quarter, primarily due to rising raw material and fuel expenses. Nevertheless, there was a slight revenue increase of approximately ten percent. Cement sale volumes rose by twelve percent, and the construction chemicals sector showed positive results.

news.title: MahaRERA invokes force majeure; extends project completion timeline by four months
news.para: Maharashtra's real estate regulator has granted a four-month extension for project completion deadlines, addressing the challenges developers face due to ongoing supply chain disruptions. This respite applies to all projects set to conclude on or after February 28, 2026, and comes in light of a Union Ministry advisory related to the consequences of the West Asia conflict.
